screening_decisions.reason: Cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study evaluating multiple biomarkers (HE4, CA125) and algorithms (ROMA, RMI) in women with pelvic mass. Uses histological confirmation as reference standard. Compares test combinations and evaluates accuracy separately in premenopausal and postmenopausal women.

Prospective cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA in women with pelvic mass. Uses final pathologic results as reference standard. Evaluates test combinations and differentiates between endometriosis and carcinoma.

Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study validating the ADNEX multivariable model (combining ultrasound and CA125) in women with adnexal masses. Uses histopathological diagnosis as reference standard. Evaluates model with and without CA125 inclusion.

Retrospective case note audit examining CA125 usage patterns in clinical practice. NOT a diagnostic test accuracy study - does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy against a reference standard in women with pelvic mass suspicious for OC. Population includes patients with various conditions and both sexes.

Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study externally validating the ADNEX model and comparing with other models (simple rules, LR2, RMI) in women with adnexal masses. Uses pathology as reference standard. Evaluates multiple test combinations.

Systematic review and meta-analysis, NOT a primary diagnostic test accuracy study. Selection criteria specify cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy studies, randomised trials, or studies validating multivariable models - not secondary analyses of existing studies.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating multiple RMI variants (1, 2, 3, 4) combining ultrasound, menopausal status, and CA125 in women with adnexal masses. Uses histopathologic results as reference standard. Compares test performance in premenopausal and postmenopausal women.

Prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study comparing HE4, CA125, and ROMA in women with benign pelvic mass and epithelial ovarian cancer. Evaluates diagnostic accuracy according to menopausal status and stages. Includes healthy controls and other disease participants for specificity evaluation.

Cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study comparing HE4, CA125, and ROMA in women with benign and malignant gynaecological diseases. Evaluates differential diagnosis of benign gynaecological diseases versus malignant ovarian cancer. Uses histological confirmation.

Systematic review about symptoms of ovarian cancer, NOT a diagnostic test accuracy study. Does not evaluate ultrasound, biomarkers, or test combinations against a reference standard in women with pelvic mass suspicious for OC.

Systematic review and meta-analysis, NOT a primary diagnostic test accuracy study. Selection criteria specify primary studies (cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy studies, randomised trials, or model validation studies) - not secondary analyses.

Epidemiological/statistical report on global cancer burden. NOT a diagnostic test accuracy study. Does not evaluate any diagnostic tests, ultrasound, biomarkers, or test combinations for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study developing and validating the ADNEX multivariable model (combining age, CA-125, ultrasound features) in women with ovarian masses. Uses histological classification as reference standard. Validates multivariable model for test combinations.

Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study comparing CA-125, HE4, RMI-II, and ROMA in women with adnexal neoplasia. Uses histological diagnosis as reference standard. Evaluates performance separately in premenopausal and postmenopausal women.

Prospective case-control diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4 and CA125 alone and in combination, plus ROMA algorithm, in women with adnexal mass. Evaluates diagnostic accuracy with histological confirmation. Compares test combinations.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4 and ROMA in women with benign cysts, endometriosis, and EOC. Uses histological confirmation as reference standard. Evaluates diagnostic accuracy separately in premenopausal and postmenopausal women. Also includes prognostic analysis.

Prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study comparing IOTA strategies (LR1, LR2, simple rules, simple descriptors) and RMI in women with adnexal masses. Uses histology after surgery as reference standard. Compares multiple test strategies.

Diagnostic accuracy study developing and validating the RMI (combining CA125, ultrasound score, and menopausal status) in women with pelvic masses. Evaluates test combinations for preoperative diagnosis of ovarian cancer. Uses histological confirmation.

Basic science study examining HE4 protein expression using immunohistochemistry and cell culture. NOT a diagnostic test accuracy study - does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy of serum biomarkers against a reference standard in women with pelvic mass suspicious for OC.

Diagnostic accuracy study comparing CA125, HE4, and ROMA in women with malignant, benign, and borderline ovarian tumors. Evaluates diagnostic accuracy separately in premenopausal and postmenopausal women. Uses pathological examinations as reference standard.

Prospective diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4 and CA-125 and ROMA in women with cystic ovarian mass suspicious for epithelial ovarian cancer. Uses histological confirmation as reference standard. Evaluates diagnostic accuracy separately in premenopausal and postmenopausal women.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA in women with benign gynecological diseases and ovarian cancer. Uses histological confirmation as reference standard. Evaluates diagnostic accuracy separately in premenopausal and postmenopausal women.

Prospective validation study evaluating simple ultrasound rules, RMI, logistic regression models, and subjective assessment in women with adnexal masses. Uses histological classification as reference standard. Compares multiple test strategies including combinations.

Cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating ROMA (combination of HE4 and CA125 biomarkers with menopausal status) in 260 postmenopausal women with ovarian masses. Reference standard is histopathological verification. Reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV. Meets all selection criteria.
Population projections study about cancer incidence and mortality. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study. Does not evaluate diagnostic tests for ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses.
Qualitative study describing patient experiences with diagnosis. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study. Does not evaluate diagnostic tests or biomarkers.
Review article about ovarian cancer molecular pathogenesis and mouse models. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Nested case-control study evaluating biomarker changes in prediagnostic serum specimens collected years before diagnosis. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study in women with symptomatic pelvic masses. Study design and population do not match selection criteria.
Methodological paper describing a quality assessment tool for systematic reviews. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Validation study of ROMA algorithm (multivariable model using CA125, HE4, and menopausal status) in 207 women with pelvic masses. Reference standard is definitive histologic diagnosis. Meets selection criteria for studies validating multivariable models.
Literature review about CA125 characteristics and clinical significance. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.
Review article proposing a model for ovarian cancer development. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.
Review article about proteomic technologies in ovarian cancer. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating RMI (combination of ultrasound, CA125, and menopausal status) in 540 women with adnexal masses. Reference standard is histopathological findings. Reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV stratified by menopausal status. Meets all selection criteria.

Diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating ROMA in 443 patients with pelvic masses. Reference standard is biopsy or clinical follow-up with imaging. Reports sensitivity and specificity. Meets selection criteria.

Cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating expert sonography, CA-125, RMI, and combinations in 1362 women with adnexal masses. Reference standard is histopathology from surgical exploration. Compares multiple test combinations stratified by menopausal status. Meets all selection criteria.

Prospective multicenter cross-sectional study validating IOTA ultrasound strategy in 1165 women with adnexal masses. Reference standard is histological diagnosis from surgery. Reports sensitivity and specificity. Meets selection criteria for diagnostic test accuracy studies.
Methodological paper about publication bias tests in meta-analyses of diagnostic accuracy. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA in 756 patients with pelvic masses. Reports AUC for different biomarkers. Meets selection criteria for diagnostic test accuracy studies evaluating biomarkers and test combinations.

External validation study of ADNEX multivariable model in 327 patients with adnexal masses. Reference standard is histological diagnosis. Reports sensitivity and specificity. Meets selection criteria for studies validating multivariable models.

Cohort study evaluating implementation of symptom-triggered testing guidance. Focuses on referral patterns and outcomes, not diagnostic test accuracy. Does not evaluate specific diagnostic tests or their accuracy.

Prospective multicenter study validating a predictive model using HE4 and CA125 in 531 patients with pelvic masses. Reference standard is histological diagnosis from surgery. Reports sensitivity and specificity stratified by menopausal status. Meets selection criteria for studies validating multivariable models.
Clinical practice guidelines document. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.
Molecular genetics study about ARID1A mutations in ovarian cancer. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study.
Abstract is incomplete/truncated. Cannot verify if study meets selection criteria. Conservative decision to exclude.

Prospective multicenter diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating HE4 and ROMA in 414 women with adnexal masses. Reference standard is histological diagnosis from surgery. Reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV. Meets all selection criteria.

This is an epidemiological study investigating long-term trends in incidence of borderline tumors and ovarian cancer in Sweden. It does not evaluate diagnostic test accuracy for ovarian cancer diagnosis in women with pelvic masses.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of existing literature, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study. The review objective is to establish accuracy of diagnostic tests in primary studies, not reviews.

Prospective trial evaluating ROMA, HE4, and CA125 for prediction of adnexal mass malignancy in pre- and post-menopausal women. Uses pathological results as reference standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.

Prospective multicentre cross-sectional study evaluating IOTA prediction models (LR2, SR), RMI, and subjective assessment for preoperative characterisation of adnexal masses. Uses surgical findings and histological diagnosis as reference standard. Meets selection criteria.
This is a meta-analysis of 32 studies evaluating diagnostic markers, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study. The review includes primary studies, not meta-analyses.

Prospective cross-sectional study evaluating CA-125, RMI, HE4, and ROMA in patients with ovarian lesions. Uses histopathological diagnosis as gold standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.

Multicenter study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA performance in differential diagnosis of epithelial ovarian cancer in patients with suspicious pelvic mass requiring surgery. Uses surgical identification as reference standard. Meets selection criteria.

This is a methodological paper describing a hierarchical regression model for meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy studies. It does not present primary diagnostic test accuracy data for ovarian cancer.

This is a methodological paper investigating performance of meta-analysis models with few studies or sparse data. It does not present primary diagnostic test accuracy data for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

This is a genetic study identifying germ-line mutations in tumor suppressor genes in women with ovarian carcinoma. It does not evaluate diagnostic test accuracy for ovarian cancer diagnosis in symptomatic women with pelvic masses.
This is a review article summarizing current strategies for prevention, detection, and treatment of ovarian cancer. It is not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Prospective multicenter blinded clinical trial validating ROMA in women presenting with pelvic mass. Uses HE4 and CA125 biomarkers with histopathological confirmation. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.

Prospective study evaluating four risk of malignancy indices (RMI 1, 2, 3, 4) for detection of malignant ovarian tumors in women with pelvic masses. Uses surgical exploration as reference. Meets selection criteria.

Study evaluating RMI, CA-125, and inflammatory markers (NLR, PLR) for discriminating ovarian cancers in postmenopausal women with adnexal masses. Uses surgical diagnosis as reference. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.

Study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA in preoperative differentiation of benign and malignant adnexal masses in pre- and postmenopausal women. Uses histopathological diagnosis as reference. Meets selection criteria.

This is a population-based case-control study identifying symptoms of ovarian cancer in primary care. It does not evaluate diagnostic test accuracy of ultrasound or biomarkers in women with pelvic masses.

Prospective validation study of ROMA algorithm using HE4 and CA125 in women with pelvic mass scheduled for surgery. Uses histopathological diagnosis as reference. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic models for preoperative identification of malignant disease. It is not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Study comparing CA125, HE4, ROMA, and RMI for differentiating between malignant and benign ovarian masses. Uses imaging analyses and histopathological diagnosis as reference. Meets selection criteria for comparing multiple tests.
This is a clinical practice statement/guideline on risk assessment for inherited gynecologic cancer predispositions. It is not a diagnostic test accuracy study.

Cross-sectional study evaluating CA-125, HE4, and ROMA at standard and optimal cut-offs for preoperative prediction of epithelial ovarian carcinoma in Vietnam. Uses histopathological diagnosis as reference. Meets selection criteria.

Study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA index for primary detection of ovarian cancer in postmenopausal women with adnexal masses. Uses histologically verified diagnoses as reference. Meets selection criteria.

Study evaluating 2D ultrasound, 3DPD ultrasound, CA125, RMI, IOTA simple rules, expert opinion, and LR2 for predicting malignant or benign nature of pelvic masses in postmenopausal women. Uses histopathological results as reference. Meets selection criteria.

This is a systematic review/meta-analysis comparing HE4 and CA-125, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. The selection criteria specify cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy studies, randomised trials, or studies validating multivariable models - not systematic reviews.

This is a diagnostic study evaluating HE4, CA-125, and ROMA in 129 patients with pelvic masses suspected of ovarian origin scheduled for surgery or radiological-guided biopsy (implying histological reference standard). It compares multiple tests and validates a multivariable model (ROMA) for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Prospective diagnostic accuracy study comparing HE4, CA125, ROMA, and RMI in 50 women with complex pelvic masses. Pre-operative evaluation implies histological confirmation after surgery. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.

This is a methodology paper describing a risk of bias assessment tool (PROBAST), not a diagnostic accuracy study for ovarian cancer. It does not evaluate any diagnostic tests in women with pelvic masses.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating ROMA (multivariable model combining HE4 and CA125) in 104 women with pelvic masses (55 EOC, 49 benign) scheduled for surgery. Reference standard is histological diagnosis. Meets criteria for validating multivariable models for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

This is an administrative data study examining routes to cancer diagnosis in England, not a diagnostic test accuracy study for ovarian cancer. It does not evaluate specific diagnostic tests with histological reference standard in women with pelvic masses.

This is a methodology paper discussing meta-analysis techniques for diagnostic accuracy studies, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study for ovarian cancer. It reanalyzes data from a published meta-analysis.

Prospective diagnostic accuracy study comparing RMI, ROMA, CA125, and HE4 in 901 women (784 evaluable) with pelvic masses scheduled for surgery. Reference standard is histological diagnosis. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.
This is a software user guide for meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy studies, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study for ovarian cancer. It does not evaluate any diagnostic tests.
This is a meta-analysis of 11 studies comparing ROMA, HE4, and CA125, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. The selection criteria specify primary studies, not systematic reviews or meta-analyses.

Diagnostic accuracy study using IOTA database of 2445 patients with adnexal masses, evaluating IOTA logistic regression models (LR1, LR2), simple rules, and RMI. Reference standard is histological diagnosis of surgically removed adnexal masses. Meets criteria for validating multivariable models.

Subset analysis from prospective trial evaluating CA-125 and HE4 in 229 premenopausal women with adnexal masses undergoing surgery. Reference standard is histological diagnosis. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study comparing two tests.

This study focuses on prognosis and therapy-monitoring of EOC, not diagnosis. It evaluates HE4 for predicting recurrence and prognosis after treatment, not for diagnosing ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses suspicious for cancer.

This study only includes women with benign gynecological disorders (1042 patients), with no cancer cases. It cannot evaluate diagnostic accuracy for ovarian cancer as there is no comparison group with confirmed ovarian cancer.
This is a review article discussing biomarkers for ovarian cancer, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. It does not present original data evaluating diagnostic tests.

Diagnostic accuracy study developing and validating HE4 ELISA test in postmenopausal patients with ovarian carcinoma and controls. Compares HE4 to CA125 with histological confirmation. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study.

This is a systematic review of 109 accuracy studies on prediction models for ovarian malignancy, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. The selection criteria specify primary studies, not systematic reviews.

This study evaluates sentinel lymph node biopsy for endometrial cancer, not ovarian cancer. The population and cancer type do not match the selection criteria which specify ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses.

This is primarily a meta-analysis of 7 studies (including a validation study) on IOTA simple rules. While it includes a validation component, the primary focus is meta-analysis, which is not within the selection criteria for primary diagnostic accuracy studies.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating CA125, HE4, and ROMA in 762 patients with benign gynecological disease and 70 with ovarian cancer. Calculates AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.
This is a review article comparing multiple diagnostic models and indices for ovarian cancer, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. It does not present original data from a single study.

Multicenter diagnostic accuracy study validating RMI, ROMA, CA125, and HE4 in 638 women with ovarian cysts or pelvic tumors. Reference standard is final pathology report. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests and validating multivariable models.

Diagnostic accuracy study comparing ADNEX model with subjective assessment in 353 patients with adnexal masses undergoing surgery. Reference standard is histological diagnosis. Meets criteria for validating multivariable models for ovarian cancer diagnosis.
